article_title: Modelling Human Teaching Tactics and Strategies for Tutoring Systems: 14 Years On
citation: Benedict du Boulay & Rosemary Luckin. (2015). Modelling Human Teaching Tactics and Strategies for Tutoring Systems: 14 Years On. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-015-0053-0
title: Akhras and Self's four properties of constructivist learning interaction sequences
description: Under Akhras and Self's view of Constructivism, teaching emphasises "the process rather than the product of learning", and intelligent learning environments evaluate learning according to four properties of constructivist learning processes: cumulativeness, constructiveness, self-regulatedness, and reflectiveness. These properties describe sequences of learning interactions and inform decisions about the learning opportunities provided to learners, taking into account the affordances of learning situations. The review presents this as an example of teaching strategies derived from epistemological learning theories.
requirements: Learning environments must be able to evaluate learning interactions according to the four properties to make decisions about learning opportunities
constraints: The framework is presented as one constructivist view among several overlapping theory-derived strategies in the review
target_learning_goals: constructivist learning processes including self-regulation and reflection
examples: Cumulativeness involves the same entity being experienced more than once in a sequence; constructiveness involves entities experienced earlier being related to new entities the learner generates later
